record.what_it_does: Intapp DealCloud: CRM and deal management platform for financial services and private capital firms.
record.auth_notes: The REST API uses the OAuth2 client credentials flow. An admin creates the client ID and secret per tenant site. The token endpoint is {baseUrl}/api/rest/v1/oauth/token. Scopes are data, user_management, publish, ri_import and backup. Tokens expire after 15 minutes. The MCP server uses per-user OAuth 2.0 with .well-known discovery, so no client ID or secret is needed. A multi-user toolkit would use the per-user OAuth through MCP, or per-customer client credentials against the REST API.
record.access_notes: DealCloud is an enterprise product with no public pricing or free tier that I found. The API is per-tenant: a customer's DealCloud admin must issue API keys (client ID and secret) on that customer's site. A developer cannot get credentials alone without a licensed tenant. I did not find a public developer sandbox signup, and I did not open a pricing or access page, so this rests on inference.
record.api_breadth_notes: Documented areas are Schema, Data (cells, rows, history, files, delete, merge, template reports), User Management, Publications, Site Backups, Relationship Intelligence import, and Schema Contracts. SDKs exist for Python and C#. The data model is dynamic and varies by tenant.
record.mcp_notes: The docs have an MCP section (api.docs.dealcloud.com/mcp/authentication and /mcp/connections) covering OAuth connections for AI clients. I did not see the server URL on the pages I fetched. It is probably tenant-specific.
record.blocker_notes: The docs are public, but credentials are issued by a customer's DealCloud admin on a licensed tenant, so a developer cannot sign up alone. Each customer would need to generate client credentials, or use the vendor's per-user MCP OAuth. The official MCP server is a possible route, but whether a third-party platform can use it is unconfirmed.
